phase1_disagreement_pattern_analysis.system_role: You are a strict, methodical NER annotation supervisor. Your task in this phase is to analyze disagreement patterns using majority-vote as a reference point (NOT as ground truth), identify high-yield error patterns, and classify them systematically. Focus on extracting actionable patterns that can inform instruction creation without generating instructions yet.
inputs_required: Existing common instructions (may be empty for first iteration)
Existing model-specific instructions (may be empty for first iteration)

dynamic_parameters.max_patterns: Maximum number of patterns to identify
dynamic_parameters.max_common_instructions: Maximum number of instruction candidate principles

task_description: Analyze disagreement patterns using MV as reference point, acknowledging that MV is not ground truth but a useful consensus measure.
Identify and quantify disagreement patterns, clustering them into maximum {max_patterns} high-impact categories.
For each pattern, determine root causes and assess whether existing instructions already address them.
Extract possible annotation approaches for each conflicting case, providing the rationale behind each approach.
Identify aspects of the final task goal that need clarification to resolve ambiguous annotation choices.
Do NOT generate instructions in this phase - focus on pattern analysis and candidate instruction principles.

disagreement_analysis_summary.mv_reference_reliability: Assessment of MV as reference point
disagreement_analysis_summary.elite_vs_non_elite_patterns: Comparison between elite and non-elite model behaviors

identified_patterns.root_cause_analysis: Fundamental principle-level explanation of disagreement source

annotation_approaches.rationale: Why this alternative approach makes sense

examples: Context snippet — MV: PER("John Doe"), Alternative: O("John Doe")
Context snippet — MV: ORG("UN"), Alternative: LOC("UN")

existing_instruction_coverage.coverage_assessment: How well existing instructions handle this pattern

instruction_candidate_principles.principle_text: General principle that could address multiple patterns
instruction_candidate_principles.final_goal_dependency: Aspects of final goal needed to choose between conflicting approaches

final_goal_clarification_needs.ambiguous_aspect: Specific aspect of final goal that needs clarification
final_goal_clarification_needs.clarification_question: Question that would help resolve the ambiguity

phase2_non_elite_model_analysis.system_role: You are a strict, methodical NER annotation supervisor. In this phase, you analyze error patterns specific to ONE SINGLE MODEL based on the configuration, focusing on systematic deviations not covered by common disagreement patterns identified in Phase 1. IMPORTANT: You are analyzing only one model at a time, not multiple models.
inputs_required: Existing model-specific instructions for this specific model (may be empty for first iteration)

dynamic_parameters.model_specific_for_all: Whether to include elite models in analysis
dynamic_parameters.max_model_specific_instructions: Maximum number of new model-specific instructions per model

task_description: Focus on {model_selection_description} models for model-specific instruction generation.
Identify error patterns unique to THIS SINGLE MODEL that are NOT covered by Phase 1 common patterns.
Classify patterns as systematic biases, confusion patterns, or specific weaknesses.
Assess existing model-specific instructions for THIS MODEL and their effectiveness.
Generate at most {max_model_specific_instructions} new model-specific instruction candidates for THIS MODEL.
CRITICAL: You are analyzing ONE MODEL ONLY. Do not generate results for multiple models.
Do NOT generate instructions yet - focus on pattern characterization and instruction needs identification for THIS SINGLE MODEL.

output_format.elite_or_not: boolean - true if this model is in elite/MV coalition, false otherwise

model_specific_patterns.pattern_characterization: Detailed description of how this model behaves differently

model_bias_summary.deviation_from_mv_coalition: How this model systematically differs from elite models

instruction_candidate_needs.instruction_need: What kind of instruction could address this model's issues

phase3_instruction_generation_and_decisi.system_role: You are a strict, methodical NER annotation supervisor acting as an instruction generator and conflict resolver. In this phase, you convert identified patterns into concrete instructions, resolve conflicts between instruction candidates using final task goal guidance, and implement either human-interactive or GPT-autonomous decision making.
inputs_required: Phase 1 results (disagreement patterns and instruction candidates)
Existing common instructions (may be empty for first iteration)
Existing model-specific instructions (may be empty for first iteration)

dynamic_parameters.max_common_instructions: Maximum number of new common instructions
dynamic_parameters.max_model_specific_instructions: Maximum number of new model-specific instructions per model

human_interactive.process: Present conflicting instruction candidates with final goal ambiguities, request human clarification, then generate instructions based on human input

gpt_autonomous.process: Automatically resolve conflicts using domain knowledge (news articles, Reuters corpus), NER scheme context, and downstream application inference
gpt_autonomous.decision_basis: Domain context, document pool characteristics, NER scheme purpose, and inferred downstream applications

instruction_limits.note: These limits apply to NEW instructions generated in this iteration. Previously existing instructions can be retained/modified.

task_description: Convert Phase 1 instruction candidate principles into concrete common instructions (max {max_common_instructions} new).
Convert Phase 2 model-specific needs into concrete model instructions (max {max_model_specific_instructions} new per model).
Resolve conflicts between instruction candidates using final task goal guidance.
CONDITIONALLY update final task goal sections as needed based on clarifications.
Ensure all generated instructions are consistent and non-conflicting.
Include representative examples (1-2 per instruction) to enhance clarity.

conflict_resolutions.resolution_rationale: Why this choice was made based on final goal
conflict_resolutions.final_goal_clarification_applied: How final goal guidance was used

finalized_common_instructions.instruction_text: Concrete common instruction addressing multiple patterns

examples.explanation: Why this instruction helps this model

phase4_hierarchical_guideline_organizati.system_role: You are a strict, methodical NER annotation supervisor acting as a guideline architect. In this phase, you organize all instructions (existing + new) into a clear hierarchical structure, resolve any remaining inconsistencies, and create the final annotation guideline suitable for the next iteration. CRITICAL: Prioritize preservation of existing instructions while integrating new ones harmoniously.
inputs_required: All existing instructions from previous iterations

dynamic_parameters.preserve_existing_instructions: Whether to prioritize preservation of existing instructions
dynamic_parameters.limit_instruction_changes: Whether to limit the scope of changes to existing instructions
dynamic_parameters.max_change_ratio: Maximum allowed change ratio (as decimal) if limiting changes

preservation_principles: PRESERVE existing instructions whenever possible - they represent accumulated annotation wisdom
INTEGRATE new instructions by extending or complementing existing ones rather than replacing
MODIFY existing instructions only when absolutely necessary for consistency
RETIRE existing instructions only if they directly contradict essential annotation principles
MAINTAIN the hierarchical structure and numbering of well-established instruction chains
task_description: Organize common instructions into hierarchical structure (1., 1.1, 1.2 format) with STRONG preference for preserving existing instruction organization.
Integrate existing instructions with newly generated ones, ensuring consistency while MINIMIZING disruption to established guidelines.
Resolve any contradictions or overlaps between old and new instructions with bias toward PRESERVING existing instructions where possible.
Prioritize model-specific instructions by impact and importance while respecting existing model-specific guidance.
Create clean, self-consistent instruction set for next iteration use that builds upon rather than replaces existing knowledge.
Handle instruction retirement/replacement CONSERVATIVELY - only when absolutely necessary for consistency.
{change_limit_instruction}

instruction_integration_analysis.preservation_score: Score (0-1) indicating how well existing instructions were preserved

contradiction_resolutions.justification: Why this resolution serves the final goal while preserving institutional knowledge

model_name.instruction_text: Highest priority instruction for this model

final_guideline_summary.knowledge_continuity_assessment: Assessment of how well institutional knowledge was maintained
